---
title: "Session 10 guided lab"
subtitle: "Translate one R analysis into Python"
---

::: {.callout-note}
**Suggested use:** tasks 1–9 are the core R-to-Python translation. Additional
practice extends the same analysis with copying, reshaping, functions, exports,
and equivalence checks and may be completed independently.
:::

Copy `starter/python-intro.py` to `work/session10/` and open the copy in Positron.

## Tasks

1. Select the course Python interpreter and run the setup cell.
2. Inspect the DataFrame shape, column types, head, key uniqueness, and missingness.
3. Select week-4 rows without dropping missing markers.
4. Produce total `n`, observed `n`, mean, and SD by arm with pandas.
5. Verify total and observed counts using a second simple Python expression.
6. Compare the pandas output with the supplied R reference values.
7. Create one clearly labelled diagnostic plot.
8. Restart the interpreter and run every cell in order.
9. Add the required AI-use disclosure as a final comment.

## Additional practice: complete a second translation

1. Create `week4_safe` using `.loc[...].copy()`. Modify a new column and explain
   why an explicit copy makes the intent clearer than a chained assignment.
2. Reshape baseline and week-4 marker into one row per participant, then calculate
   change while retaining participants with missing week-4 values.
3. Write `summarize_week(data, week)` that validates required columns and returns
   total `n`, observed `n`, mean, and SD by arm.
4. Test the function on the supplied data, an absent week, and a copy in which one
   arm is entirely missing at week 4.
5. Reproduce the participant-level change calculation in R or compare it with
   supplied R reference values. Use an explicit numerical tolerance.
6. Export the participant-level table to CSV, read it back with pandas, and compare
   dimensions, key uniqueness, missingness, and numeric values.
7. Create a second diagnostic figure showing baseline versus follow-up with an
   identity line and arm-specific encodings.
8. Restart the interpreter and run all cells in order. Record one Python state or
   indexing mistake that the clean run exposed.

### Independent-practice check

The participant table must have one row per ID and preserve both missing week-4
values. The function must retain total group size when all marker values are
missing.

## Exit evidence

Submit the completed `.py` file and a short text or Quarto note containing the
comparison, missing-value explanation, and disclosure.
